Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

Nestimate 1.1.3

Changes since the CRAN release 0.9.24.

Breaking: results with a new shape

These results are now tidy data frames, one row per observation, with a group column where there are groups. format = "wide" returns the old one-column-per-group table; summary() returns every row as a plain data frame, and print() shows the first n rows.

  • sequence_metrics(group = ): one row per index and group, with the difference, Hedges’ g and its interval, eta squared and p-values.
  • sequence_patterns(group = ): one row per pattern and group, with group_support.
  • net_centrality() of a group of networks: one data frame with group and state columns; it returned a list of data frames.
  • summary() of a grouped network: one row per metric and group.
  • summary() of passage_time(), transition_entropy() and chain_structure() returns one data frame; table = gives the second table ("pairs", "chain", "absorption"). They returned a list. Grouped results stack the table with a group column.
  • summary() of markov_stability() returns the table and prints nothing.
  • vertex_compare() names its columns observed_x and observed_y.
  • summary(nct(), table = "edges") returns the edge table; nct() stores the M and S tests as $structure and $strength.
  • print() of a network lists its strongest edges instead of the weight matrix.

Rerun an analysis made with 0.9.24 if it uses

  • data whose column roles came from their names, or long-log times not in a whole format with a four-digit year. Declare action, actor, time, state_cols, metadata_cols or cols; one-hot data needs format = "onehot" or codes.
  • wide data with metadata, actor, time or order columns, which were read as states.
  • permutation() or compare_networks(test = "permutation") on networks built with different estimator settings (say Pearson and Spearman): the difference was reported as a difference between the groups. Such pairs are now refused.
  • boot_glasso(), build_mcml_pc() or loading_stability(): they now use the network’s own estimator settings.
  • casedrop_reliability() or centrality_stability(): failed subsets count as below threshold, and casedrop_reliability() compares only the existing edges of a transition network (target = "all" gives the earlier values).
  • build_mogen() or markov_order_test(): dof = "paths" is the default (dof = "observed" gives the earlier values).
  • build_hon(method = "hon"), which now follows pyHON, or build_hypa(), whose null is strength-preserving (the earlier null flagged anomalies in first-order data).
  • nct(), whose $structure and $strength held each other’s values in 0.9.24, or strengths from summary(), whose in and out spreads were swapped.
  • build_mlvar() temporal edges, which now run from predictor to outcome.
  • sequence_compare() effect sizes, which depended on min_freq.
  • predict_links() ties, evaluate_links(), scaling = "normalize" on an undirected network (now directed when the result is asymmetric) or the kernel width of landscape_surface() and landscape_trend().
  • corrected estimates in centrality (BetweennessRSP, betweenness ties, min-max normalisation), net_prune(), build_mmm(), build_clusters(), build_mcml(), passage_time(), chain_structure(), markov_stability(), entropy_bayes(), hypergraph_centrality(), q_analysis(), persistent_homology(), betti_numbers(), bottleneck_distance(), pathways(), mogen_transitions(), extract_initial_probs() and mosaic_analysis().

New features

  • build_network(method = "latency"): a reply network weighted by reply speed (Templeton et al. 2022).
  • tna and group_tna models are accepted wherever a network or sequences are.
  • stability_landscape(), landscape_surface() and landscape_trend() draw a transition network as a ball-in-cup landscape.
  • extract_sequences(), sequence_patterns(), sequence_metrics() and pattern_outcome(): the sequences, patterns and indices behind any input. sequence_metrics() compares every index between groups, within actors when an actor appears in several groups.
  • mark_phases() splits each actor’s events into n phases, for build_network(group = "phase").
  • mosaic_test(), and nested, actor and report in mosaic_plot() and mosaic_analysis(), for counts nested in actors.
  • node_clusters(), label_predictions() and label_scores().
  • actor drops whole actors in centrality_stability() and casedrop_reliability(), and takes nested levels in permutation().
  • entropy_trajectory() reads sequences as well as an event log, and its plot() draws a bootstrap confidence band around each trend.
  • sequence_plot() gains periods (weeks or months), period_unit and fill; it and distribution_plot() gain cols and a two-part trim.
  • extract_edges() and extract_initial_probs() read a group of networks; summary() of magnitude_difference() returns its edges.
  • compare_networks() stars the tested differences in plot(type = "difference").
  • nct() gains na_method and accepts missing values and constant variables.
  • build_network(params = list(window_size = )) counts sequences between blocks of positions, as tna::tna() does (it was ignored).
  • The build_*() shortcuts take group, scaling, threshold and params as named arguments; build_mcml() gains from, to, weight and cols; cooccurrence() and association_rules() gain format = "binary".
  • New dataset daily_actions.

Other changes

  • print() of sequence_compare() shows one row per pattern and group, rounded, with a group column; summary(format = "long") returns that table for every pattern. The result and summary() keep their shape.
  • One colour rule for states: with no colours set, every figure draws the states in Okabe-Ito colours dealt in alphabetical order, and objects derived from a network keep its palette. The clusters of an mcml and the groups of an entropy_trajectory() plot take the colours the states leave. plot_state_frequencies(colors = ) is now state_colors = (colors still works, with a warning).
  • Plots that used ggplot’s default hues, viridis or green and red use Okabe-Ito and the package’s blue-red diverging colours, with shapes or linetypes where colour alone told groups apart.
  • Sequence verbs refuse one-hot and association networks; resampling verbs refuse one-sequence data and networks built with level, and all but bootstrap_network() refuse latency networks; Markov measures refuse correlation networks.
  • entropy_trajectory() refuses a time column with missing values.
  • prepare_onehot() and plot_mosaic() are no longer exported.
  • sequence_plot() arguments after group must be named.
  • seed = no longer moves the session’s random stream.

Bug fixes

  • plot() of entropy_trajectory() dropped a group with few windows; it is now drawn as its windows and named in a warning.
  • plot() of bayes_compare() on a group of networks failed.
  • build_network() stored averaged metadata as a one-dimensional array, so landscape_trend(along = ) failed.
  • Colours set with set_state_colors() were lost by build_clusters(), build_mmm(), cluster_network() and other derived objects, and were matched against the wrong name column.
  • subset() of compare_networks() tables printed at two decimals.
  • One-state data failed in bootstrap_network(), path_dependence() and predict_links().
  • labels = did not relabel stored data.
  • sequence_plot() and distribution_plot() refused a data.table or tibble.
  • cluster_network() did not pass its arguments.
  • build_hon(method = "hon+") missed some higher-order rules.
  • The pyramid plot of sequence_compare() cut off its counts.

Nestimate 0.9.24

CRAN release: 2026-10-07

Documentation

  • Fixes to the 0.9.23 help-page merge, found in review:
    • Pages are named after their function again: build_mcml and plot_state_frequencies had been named after a print() method, and their usage now lists the function before its methods.
    • The descriptions of 51 methods (what a plot draws, what a print shows) are restored, as a “Methods” section on each function’s page.
    • Each page’s ... entry states what each method does with extra arguments: methods that reject them say so, plot.net_bayes() names cograph::splot(), and the rest say they are ignored.
    • compare_networks: the ... and labels entries no longer repeat; net_edge_betweenness and net_pruning_details no longer list a non-existent class.
    • Every S3 method has a documented return value.

Behaviour notes

  • The mgm estimator rejects scale = FALSE with a classed error (nestimate_mgm_unscaled); this started in 0.9.23 and was not listed there. Missing values are handled pairwise, now passed explicitly.

Tests

  • Two more reference-implementation tests (a hand-written linear solve for passage_time(), a manual multinom re-computation) and unused reference helpers moved to the local suite; section headers that claimed equivalence tests are renamed. New tests: mgm on data with missing values, and the scale = FALSE error.
